title: Quant
text:
Part I: Intro to Quant Finance. A basic introduction to mathematical finance that builds intuition by pricing assets in discrete time. This follows the module ST339, taught by Vicky Henderson at the University of Warwick. See the notes.
Part II: Continuous-time Finance. This extends the ideas and intuition from the discrete case to continuous time. It follows the module ST401, taught by Gechun Liang at the University of Warwick. See the notes.



Alongside the theory, I aim to cover practical quant finance topics such as:

Backtesting
Trading strategies
Performance metrics




Projects bring together both the theory and application into self-contained examples. Some may be just one jupyter notebook and other’s could be its own repo.
The aim for the projects is to have one for each stage of learning so that after finishing a course you can apply the ideas into one project.

Reading list

Mathematical Finance: A Very Short Introduction by Mark H. A. Davis. A fun way to get a feel for the basic ideas.
Stochastic Calculus for Finance I: The Binomial Asset Pricing Model by Steven E. Shreve.
Stochastic Calculus for Finance II: Continuous-Time Models by Steven E. Shreve.
Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives by John C. Hull.
Arbitrage Theory in Continuous Time by Tomas Björk.

title: Part I: Intro to Quant Finance
text:
This course is an introduction to mathematical finance, built around pricing assets in discrete-time. It loosely follows the Warwick module ST339 (Vicky Henderson), supported by two textbooks:

Stochastic Finance: An Introduction in Discrete Time by Hans Föllmer and Alexander Schied
Stochastic Calculus for Finance I: The Binomial Asset Pricing Model by Steven E. Shreve
Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives by John C. Hull

title: Part II: Continuous-time Finance
text:
This course builds upon the ideas in Part I and extends them to continuous-time.It loosely follows the Warwick module ST401 (Gachun Liang), supported by two textbooks:

Stochastic Calculus for Finance II: Continuous-Time Models by Steven E. Shreve.
Arbitrage Theory in Continuous Time by Tomas Björk.

title: About
text:
My name is Grant and I am a mathematics student at the University of Warwick, interested in quantitative finance and machine learning.
I started this site as a place to organise what I’m learning, and I hope it’s useful to others who are curious about the subject too.
